segmentation.text: Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions
shall pass each other keeping to the right,
upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction,
each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the paved portion of the highway

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, for the subject and the other. 'proceeding in opposite directions': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing'; its exclusion concerns the direction of approach to an intersection, which these words do not name. 'proceeding': the subject is not at rest (negation of drv.motion.complete_halt). 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction': st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', and st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction', at most the stated figure, read on the lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies) on a highway (st.highway) it occupies.

'one-half of the paved portion of the highway': the half on the subject's side of st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', of the way the subject is on (st.on_way, 'the public way … a structure region lies on'). 'give to the other': the subject's body stays on its own half: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line from the subject ('signed lateral offset … left positive') is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent). 'the other' is the oncoming vehicle met: it closes on the subject within a horizon (prim.closest_approach_within, centres under constant velocities, not a contact or clearance) or is alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap).

operationalizations.convention: The subject gives the other half of the paved portion as nearly as possible where its body crosses the centre line by no more than a lateral positioning tolerance p.lateral_position_tolerance, or where its body is already within that tolerance of the road edge on its right (st.road_edge, ground distance through st.region_geometry, on the right per prim.region_lateral_offset), so that no more room is available to it.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) and a lane (st.lane) whose lane count in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is at most one.
obligation: For every road user c that is a vehicle, occupies the highway the subject occupies, is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_heading_cos) and is meeting it (prim.closest_approach_within(subject, c, p.meeting_horizon) or rel.longitudinal_overlap: projections share length), and for every centre line l lying on that highway (st.centre_line, st.on_way): prim.region_lateral_offset(l, subject) is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent) less p.lateral_position_tolerance, or the subject's body is within p.lateral_position_tolerance of a road edge (st.road_edge, st.region_geometry distance) lying on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset negative). Violated where neither holds.

narrowings.why: 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.

'the paved portion of the highway' is read as the roadway the centre line divides; a paved shoulder is not added to either half. Its half is given while the other vehicle approaches within p.meeting_horizon or is alongside.
'as nearly as possible' is read through the subject's room to its right road edge; obstacles on the subject's half are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane two-way road; the moving subject car straddles the centre line by 1 m while an oncoming car approaches 2 s away, with 2 m of room to its right road edge.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same road; the subject car keeps its body right of the centre line as the oncoming car passes.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives on a highway whose lane counts two lanes in its direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane road with an oncoming car approaching; the source maps regions without their outline (st.region_geometry absent), so the offset from the centre line is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives over the centre line on a two-lane road with no other vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A very narrow paved road; the subject's body crosses the centre line by 0.5 m while its right side is at the road edge, as an oncoming car passes.

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.meeting_horizon
param_proposals.convention: the time ahead within which two vehicles closing head-on on a narrow two-way road count as meeting, so that each keeps to its half: the decision-and-steering time of a driver adjusting lateral position
param_proposals.source: AASHTO decision sight distance (avoidance manoeuvre times)

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
